comments.author: @antoniobortoni
comments.text:
The good thing about AI in investing is that it doesn’t get tired, it doesn’t sleep, it moves money in seconds and spots patterns humans would never see. In theory, that’s great for everyone: smarter investments, more economic activity, more loans, and therefore more growth.

The problem is what model the banks follow:

If they use AI to give loans that strengthen society → everybody wins (win-win model, expansion, creation of real wealth).

If they use it to fund destructive projects and hoard wealth → everybody loses except them (win-lose model, typical of short-sighted elites). That doesn’t create prosperity, only debt slavery.

But even the win-win model can’t grow forever. At some point, the system has to shift to a “sustain” model: preserving what works, stabilizing what’s already big.
Otherwise, you end up with BlackRock-on-steroids, where one entity basically owns everything.

The paradox is that if AI plays the human game, it will repeat the destruction-crisis cycle that even banks suffer from. The only way it makes sense is if it plays differently: not as a predator, but as a stabilizer.
